AdmissionRefusal.description: Why a round was refused. One refused member admits no member.

ArtifactName.description: One artifact, by the store that holds it and its reference there.

ArtifactReferrerKind.description: The referrer kinds, as the `referrer_kind` column stores them.

ArtifactStoreId.description: The store that holds an artifact.

oneOf.description: A process engine's own store, by engine kind.

The immutable process-definition descriptors, keyed by their
`ProcessDefinitionId` (ADR 0113 §3.6). A collectible artifact like the
others: a descriptor lives exactly as long as some referrer holds it.

Retained tool material bundles (K2), held by Run-segment and source
leases until their last dependency ends.

A turn's recorded preparation, by digest, held by the turn journal's
`execution` referrer until the journal cannot replay (FIG-5133).

AttachmentRetentionFailure.description:
Structured attachment failure evidence. Backend diagnostics remain on the
runtime error's message; classification and refusal data remain typed.

AttachmentRetentionStoreFailure.description:
A nested store cause with the store's authoritative retry class and its
runtime code and structured refusal. The diagnostic is carried separately.

AttachmentSource.description:
The ownership-explicit attachment source at the LLM/content seam.

Inline bytes are transient and must be normalized to `Stored` before a
durable effect is emitted. Borrowed sources are never fetched by Lash and
never enter the attachment manifest.

AttachmentStoreFailureClass.description:
Why an attachment-store backend operation failed, as a property a caller can
act on without parsing the message.

The retry and operator verdicts are derived from the class, never stored
separately, so a class and its verdicts cannot contradict each other.

oneOf.description:
The operation may succeed if retried: a transport fault, timeout,
throttling, or an unclassified backend failure.

Credentials or authorization must be corrected before a retry can
succeed; the failure is operator-actionable.

The request, its configuration, or the backend's support for it cannot
succeed as written. Retrying changes nothing.

BootstrapFault.description: Why a freshly exec'd worker could not take its place on the pipe.

CancelOrigin.description:
The runtime or actor decision that requested cancellation of a process
or of a tool call's attempt. `RunClosing` is a call's owning tool Run
discharging its cancellation at Closing while the turn itself runs on.

CancelRequest.description: A process cancellation fact. Its first timestamp survives retries.

CellFailure.description: Structured failure returned by a code executor.

exec_failure.description:
Why the `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a
response, when that is the failure: the closed reason, kept typed
through the protocol driver and the trajectory it records.

tool_call_limit.description:
The session's `max_tool_calls` refusal, when that is why the cell
failed (FIG-4546), kept typed through the plugin and host result.

worker_limit.description: The measured run limit, kept typed through the plugin and host result.

CellFailureKind.description: Why an executed code cell failed.

oneOf.description: The runtime refused the program because it violates a dialect or policy bound.
The authored program failed to compile or execute correctly.
Host infrastructure failed while preparing or executing the program.

ChargeSafetyDenialReason.description:
Why host charge-safety policy denied an otherwise transport-retryable
generation.

# Integrator class

Runtime and reporting implementors exhaustively render these host-policy
outcomes; provider adapters never construct them.

oneOf.description: Host policy requires a provider idempotency or resume guarantee.
The per-call unsafe retry allowance is exhausted.
Provider-reported tokens exceed the host's duplicate-cost bound.

CompatRefusal.description:
Why a store, an epoch or a stored label is refused.

Each message names its remedy with a `lashctl` command. The JSON shape is
what `lashctl --json` reports and what a newer build reads from an older
one, so a variant's fields change only in place under the version freeze.

oneOf.description:
A SQLite database this build reads but has not migrated: its stamp is
older than the version this build writes. The store's open migrates
every database together, after a complete backup; a component opened
on its own never migrates.

`F` at open: below the writable range (a skipped release) or above it
(a newer fleet).

`F` at open: the store records no fleet epoch. The installer seeds it
and an open never does, so no build decides `F` by opening first.

A SQLite store's configured path is a directory in the retired layout
of three database files (FIG-5195). A SQLite deployment is one
database file (ADR 0132 §12), and formats reset at 1.0, so no release
migrates the old layout: the open refuses it unchanged.

files.description: The retired layout's database files the directory holds.

oneOf.description:
A stable release build refuses a store stamped before 1.0, regardless
of format counters: pre-release shapes changed in place under the freeze.

A stored label this build has no name for (an obligation state or
kind, an attachment owner kind, a referrer kind): a newer build wrote
it. Classified apart from corruption so no pass treats it as absent.

A plugin namespace is stamped with a format the fleet record does not
permit its plugin to write (FIG-4746). Nothing was published.

The fleet record carries no writer range for a plugin (FIG-4746): a
plugin the record does not name publishes only its first format.

A recorded plugin writer range is not a range (FIG-4746). The store
fails closed: no publication of that store is admitted.

A plugin writes no format the fleet record permits it (FIG-4747): an
admission chooses each plugin's writer inside its range, and this
plugin has none there. Nothing was admitted.

ConfigRefusal.description:
A refused config change: the owner it names, where it was refused and
why. Nothing of a refused change is published.

ConfigRefusalReason.description:
Why a config change was refused. Only [`Self::Owner`] carries data in the
owner's registered refusal type; every other reason is the framework's.

oneOf.description: The namespace's stored or requested writer format is unavailable.

The owner refused: `refusal` is its registered refusal type,
serialized, and `message` that refusal's display text.
No installed plugin registers the named owner.
The owner registers no command of the name the site carries.

The session recorded no namespace for the owner, so there is nothing
for the command to change.
A value did not read or write as the owner's type.

ConfigRegistrationError.description: A config registration that cannot stand.

ConfigValueRole.description:
Which value of a config judgment could not be read or written as its
owner's type.

oneOf.description: What a creator stated for the namespace.
A command's arguments.
The options a run stated for the namespace.
The namespace the owner produced: created, reduced or overridden.
A command's output.
The owner's own refusal, which did not encode.

DeclarationRefusal.description: Why a declaration, or an outcome under it, is refused.

oneOf.description: A deferring body returned a key other than the source its Run armed.

An isolated call has no inline body, so it cannot declare what only
an inline body returns.

DeclaredStartObligationRefusal.description: Why a registration cannot be a declared start.

DefinitionIdSchema.description:
The typed definition reference a durable process row pins: the engine that
owns the definition, the engine-owned definition value, and the signature
claimed for it. The claim is never authority (ADR 0095) — a peer's claim is
checked against the owning engine before any local row is created.

DefinitionRef.description:
An immutable run definition name and revision a deployment registers.

Resolution looks up the exact revision; a worker that does not serve it
retries and parks, and never falls back to another revision.

Detail.description:
A diagnostic beside a typed cause, cut to [`Self::MAX_BYTES`]. The variant
that carries it decides the class; the bound keeps a refusal within any
frame whatever its text.

DurableTraceScope.description:
The retained telemetry of one admitted scope: what caused it, the anchor
its children hang under, and when it started.

It is written once, by the admission that inserts its owner, in the same
write. Every later admission of that owner reads it back unchanged.

started_at_ms.description: Wall-clock epoch milliseconds of the first admission.

EffectAddress.description: Canonical address of one admitted runtime effect.

EffectOpener.description:
The exact logical opener that durable work binds (ADR 0099 §1).

Run admission records it, recovery validates it, and language host bridges
mint their identities under it. Every path shares the same owner value.

oneOf.description: A turn of a session.

session_id.description: The session the turn belongs to.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request.

An operation is a lifecycle owner in the sense §1 means: its id is
durable and retry-stable, so a redrive of the operation binds the
same opener. No logical turn runs under it: every turn a shift runs
is opened by its logical run's [`Turn`](Self::Turn) (FIG-3607
contract 4). A tool-bearing operation Run closes this scope on explicit
completion; tool-free administrative scopes close with their session.

operation_id.description:
The operation's durable identity. A plain string because no one
typed id names every operation; empty is refused, as
`ExecutionScope::validate` refuses an empty scope id.

session_id.description: The session the operation is on.

oneOf.description: One process.

process_id.description: The minted id of the process that owns this work.

Exchange.description: The exchange a worker answered with a message it does not admit.

oneOf.description: The first message of a checkout, which is the handshake.
A step of the run.
The parent was performing the run's request.
The run declined a park, and owed its request again.

ExecCodeFailureReason.description:
Why an `exec_code` effect failed before the executor produced a response.

This is the closed classification offline trace analysis keys on; the human
detail lives in [`ExecCodeFailure::message`]. Serialized snake_case on the
durable journal and trace surfaces.

oneOf.description: No code executor is installed on the session.
The executor's language runtime exited unexpectedly.
Any other session-layer failure; `message` carries the detail.

A journal entry written before the reason was typed: only the human
message survived the erasure, so no closed reason can be recovered.

ExecutionLease.description:
The lease one checkout of a worker runs under. The parent mints it and
fences it when the worker is lost, so a late message under an old lease is
refused rather than applied.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic
work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect
addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request. It has no
logical root, and no logical turn runs under it.

FormatRefusal.description: A plugin cannot interpret or encode this namespace's requested format.

FrameEpoch.description:
The context frame's epoch: advances when a frame opens (F5), which fences
every response from the frame before it.

FrontierRefusal.description: Why a frontier refuses a resolution.

HeaderRefusal.description: Why a receiver refused a header.

HookCause.description:
A recorded typed hook cause: a plugin's declared error type, its version
and payload. Unknown payloads survive replay unchanged.

IsolatedStartRefusal.description: A process binding that cannot honor admission.

KeyRejection.description: A deterministic rejection of a plugin-state key.

LlmProfileEffortValidationCategory.description:
Deterministic taxonomy of effort-validation failures. The serde snake_case
codes are a stable contract: downstream consumers match on them.

LlmProfileKey.description:
The host's opaque name for one registered model.

Lash never parses it: `glm-5.3-flash@tensorx` names a registration, not a
provider and a model. A session records the key with the metadata the
host's registry minted for it ([`RecordedLlmProfile`]), so the key alone never
decides how a recorded root runs.

MaterialDigest.description:
The integrity digest of the material's canonical bytes: 64 lowercase
hexadecimal digits of a BLAKE3 hash. The hashing domain belongs to the
material codec (FIG-4876), not to this reference.

oneOf.description:
In the owning Run's opener journal: resolvable within the same
segment only.

In a retained artifact store, held by a dependency lease: resolvable
across segments and deployments.

MaterialOwner.description:
Who owns a payload: the logical Run that admitted it, the process that
produced it, or the Deferred source whose seal resolved to it.

oneOf.description: The logical Run, named by its opener.
One process.
One Deferred source, named by its durable wait key.

MaterialRef.description: A typed reference to one canonical payload.

MaterialRefusal.description:
Why recorded material cannot be served: a typed retained-result failure.
None of these re-executes the body that produced the material. FIG-4876
carries it through the runtime error framework.

oneOf.description: No payload exists at the reference's location.

The payload's retention ended; an expired reference cannot restart
work.
The bytes found do not hash to the recorded digest.
The reader's owner is not the reference's owner.

The material's codec belongs to a plugin revision this build cannot
read.

MaterialRole.description:
The record that produced a payload, which is also its sole canonical
owner record: A owns the prepared request, X the attempt output and its
captures, V only presentation bytes distinct from the output.

oneOf.description: The final prepared request admission recorded (A).
One read-only namespace image shared by all admissions at its frontier.

One attempt's output and captures (X), or a cached success a
before-check supplied in its place.
Messages and observations declared by after-checks in D.
Presentation bytes distinct from the output (V).

MaxToolCalls.description:
The number of tool calls one execution may make: the host's required
decision, with no default and no built-in ceiling (FIG-4546).

What it counts depends on the execution. A cell — one code cell of a turn,
or one tool step of a protocol without cells — may make at most this many
tool calls in total. A process may hold at most this many at once: a call
counts from its acceptance until the process no longer depends on it, so
a long-running process is bounded in what it retains, never in what it
does over its life. The call that passes the limit fails with
[`ToolCallLimitExceeded`]; every call under it runs untouched. The limit
paces nothing: rate limits and throttling are the host's own.

ModuleArtifactAstRefusal.description: Owned validation evidence suitable for a worker response or a durable journal.

NamespaceFrontierRefusal.description: A frontier's refusal of a recorded resolution of one plugin's namespace.

OpaqueStateRefusal.description: Why opaque state failed a structural check.

OwnerEpoch.description:
The owner's epoch: advances when ownership of the session or durable
process moves, so a message from a superseded owner is refused.

PayloadKind.description: A typed payload inside a frame that did not encode or decode.

PluginCallbackIdentity.description:
A callback slot within one declared plugin revision. Keys are derived from
the capability kind and its registration ordinal within that plugin.

oneOf.description: The declaration names another plugin than the factory that gave it.
The plugin cannot write the format it reads natively.

PluginExecutionRefusal.description: Recorded executable requirements this build cannot fulfill.

PluginFailureClass.description: How a declared plugin failure settles, independent of its display text.

PluginFailureOrigin.description: The declared code that produced a failure. Lash stamps this at dispatch.

PluginHookFailure.description: One failed callback in registration order, including its original typed payload.

PluginOperationFailure.description: A failure whose payload remains intact when its codec is unavailable.

PluginRevision.description: The declared executable owner of a callback or tool admission.

oneOf.description:
A recorded resolution does not follow its namespace's applied
frontier: it skips a publication, or a predecessor publishes after
ownership moved on.

A reduced publication was abandoned before the engine returned it, so
whether it is durable is unknown: the namespace publishes nothing
more until it is rebuilt from durable state.

A callback returned commands where no recorded body can carry their
resolution.

PoolFault.description: A failure of the supervising pool itself, met while it drove a worker.

ProcessChangeCursor.description:
Opaque position in a store's Process Change Feed.

The wrapped sequence is meaningful only to the registry backend that issued
it. Backends expose constructors/accessors so external store implementations
can persist and bind the position, but consumers should treat values as
cursors, not comparable timestamps.

ProcessStatus.description:
Durable lifecycle status of a process row.

This enum has no `#[serde(other)]` fallback arm, by design: a store that
silently folded an unknown status into a known one would corrupt the very
fold the registry exists to keep honest.

ProtocolBreach.description:
A parent, its worker or the pool between them broke the protocol. A fresh
worker may keep it, so the owning invocation is redriven.

oneOf.description: State the worker itself produced fails the parent's structural check.
Worker code, or the parent task driving it, panicked.

ProviderFailureKind.description:
Classification of a provider/transport failure.

This is the single canonical failure-kind vocabulary: provider transports
classify failures into it (`lash-core` re-exports it from
`llm::transport`), the turn machine carries it on
[`ErrorEnvelope`](crate::session_model::ErrorEnvelope), and hosts read it
back from `TurnIssue`s without scraping traces.

`Unknown` is an explicit classification, never a decoder fallback.
Persisted failure records reject unrecognized kind literals.

ProviderFileScope.description: Provider/account boundary for a provider-owned file id.

ReasoningRefused.description:
A reasoning selection the recorded capability of the model under `key`
refuses.

ReasoningSelection.description: The host-resolved reasoning choice carried from model selection to providers.

oneOf.description: Send no reasoning control; the endpoint's own default applies.
Explicitly turn reasoning off, where the capability declares `disable`.
Request a named, capability-validated effort.

ReferrerStore.description: The byte family a referrer claims.

RefusalSite.description: Where a config refusal was raised.

oneOf.description: One command of a transaction, by its position and registered name.

The candidate as a whole: a transaction's final candidate, or the
config a run's overrides derived.
The creation of the session's namespace.
An inline-only tool declares more execution than the ceiling allows.

RemoteAbandonWriter.description: Wire mirror of the writer that established an Abandoned terminal.

RemoteAdmittedPlugin.description: Wire mirror of one plugin of a recorded plugin admission.

usage_disposition.description:
Whether `usage` was provider-reported or the attempt ended before the
provider's usage arrived (ADR 0031). Absent means reported.

RemoteEffectOpener.description:
The wire form of the shared opener vocabulary inside an owned parent.

Mirrors `lash_core::EffectOpener` arm for arm so a remote peer names the
exact durable owner — a turn, a session operation, or one process — and
never a rendered id.

RemoteGenerationReceipt.description:
Mirror of the core `GenerationReceipt`: the adapter-reported fate of a
request's generation and prompt-cache intent, so a remote host can tell an
honored repeatability request from a silently dropped one.

RemoteLeaseOwnerIdentity.description:
Wire mirror of one lease holder incarnation. Fencing identity is the full
`(owner_id, incarnation_id)` pair; neither component may be erased into an
untyped JSON carrier.

RemoteLlmCallRecord.description: Wire mirror of one logical LLM call and every provider attempt it consumed.

oneOf.description:
An origin this protocol version does not model: the runtime's
`MessageOrigin` is non-exhaustive, and a peer reading a newer
peer's origin lands here instead of failing the whole message.

RemoteOperationOutcome.description:
A host task's explicit terminal. Queued inputs are followed by their
durable input identities; their payloads remain owned by ingress.

signal_wait.description:
The wait a signal event resolves, selected by the append that
admitted the signal.

trace_cause.description: What caused the event, as the append that inserted it retained it.

segment_ordinal.description:
Execution segment the reference was minted for; absent reads as zero.
Carried so a peer's compare-and-set sees the same ordinal the owning
tier wrote, rather than silently flattening every segment to the first.

RemoteProcessHandleView.description:
A process handle as it crosses the wire.

`handle_kind` is the ADR 0095 marker field, written and required as the one
kind rather than carried as a peer-supplied string: before the cutover a
peer could send any non-empty `handle_type` and it survived validation.

RemoteProcessLifecycleState.description:
Mirrors [`lash_core::ProcessLifecycleState`]: each state owns the facts
that exist only in it, so a record cannot carry a wait beside an outcome,
or a terminal status without one.

ancestry.description: The recorded ancestry, nearest first; empty for a root start.

engine_config.description: The engine behaviour recorded at process creation.

lifecycle.description:
The one lifecycle state the process is in: its status, wait, park and
outcome are read from it and carried nowhere beside it.

lifetime.description: The recorded lifetime decision: what ends the process.

session_capability.description: The session capability the process's descendants inherit.

start_key_digest.description:
The digest of the key the process was started under, while it is
retained. It is not a caller's key: a caller that retries sends its
own raw `start_key` again, never this digest.

RemoteProcessResumeRefusal.description: Wire mirror of why a started process cannot be resumed safely.

RemoteProcessSignalRequest.description:
One signal to one process. `signal_id` is the sender's id for this one
signal: with the process and the signal name it is the signal's whole
identity, and the append that delivers it is deduplicated by that
identity alone (FIG-4299). There is no separate replay key to supply; a
request that carries one is refused, not silently re-keyed.

trace_cause.description:
What caused the signal: its producer's trace context. No part of the
signal's identity.

RemoteProcessSignalWaitBinding.description:
Wire mirror of the wait one signal event resolves: the ordinal of the
process's wait for the signal's name (FIG-4298).

RemoteProcessSignature.description:
A signature claim travelling on a definition reference, or the explicit
absence of one (ADR 0090's unknown process type).

RemoteProcessStartTarget.description:
What a remote start names to run: an executable input, or the immutable
definition one is resolved from. Mirrors
[`lash_core::ProcessStartTarget`]: a start request and a trigger target
carry it, and a process record carries the [`RemoteProcessInput`] it
resolved to.

RemoteProcessStarted.description: Wire mirror of the durable execution-started fact.

generation.description:
The executable generation the incarnation was started under
(FIG-3571), spelled as the store holds it.

plugins.description:
The plugin composition the incarnation started under, in hook order,
with the writer format chosen for each plugin (FIG-4747).

RemoteProcessTerminal.description:
Mirrors [`lash_core::ProcessTerminal`]: the outcome a process ended in,
which a terminal record and a terminal event carry. Its status is derived
from it ([`Self::status`]) and carried nowhere beside it.

forced.description:
Whether lash forced the end: a cancelled process whose engine did not
end it within its cancel grace (ADR 0132 §10).

RemoteProviderFailureKind.description: Wire mirror of the core `ProviderFailureKind` classification.

RemoteProviderRouteIdentity.description: Exact configured LLM Provider route that owns opaque replay state.

endpoint.description:
Stable routing metadata, not a secret-bearing URL. LLM Provider
endpoints reject URL userinfo; paths and query strings remain visible
in remote envelopes and traces and therefore must not carry secrets.

oneOf.description: The call's limit expired: the model total ends every further attempt.

RemoteScopeGrant.description: How a recorded lifetime's scope was granted.

RemoteScopeId.description: The wire form of a scope a process may live until: an opener or a session.

RemoteSessionTurnOutcome.description: What a remote `SessionTurn` process answers when its child turn ends.

oneOf.description: The child's assembled turn.
The child's final value, checked against `schema` when one is given.

code.description:
The stable error code of the last delivery failure: present exactly
when `last_error` is.

RemoteTerminalProcessStatus.description:
Mirrors [`lash_core::TerminalProcessStatus`]: the statuses a recorded
outcome ends a process in.

forced.description:
Whether lash forced the end: a cancelled process whose engine did not
end it within its cancel grace (ADR 0132 §10).

oneOf.description:
Observation data omits the seed bodies. The directed process-await
reply remains the lossless carrier of a frame switch.
A plugin's tool check stopped the owning Run.

owner.description: Who the intent was declared under: a session, or a process.

RemoteTriggerDeliveryFailureCode.description:
Typed provider-route refusals, with the remaining runtime vocabulary
preserved under its author namespace.

RemoteTriggerMutationReceipt.description: The admitted trigger registration result, including its recorded subscription.

RemoteTriggerProviderRoute.description: Peer projection of the authorized route a subscription pinned for its source.

RemoteTriggerSourceCapture.description: Peer projection of the source contract and route admitted at registration.

oneOf.description: Live and routable.
Live, retained, not routable.
Fenced behind a tombstone taken at the carried timestamp.

RemoteTriggerSubscriptionRecord.description:
What a trigger subscription declares (FIG-3258): the fields the draft
submits and the record retains. One struct carries them once so a field
added to one spelling cannot be dropped by the other; both DTOs embed it
flattened, leaving the wire shape unchanged.

lifecycle.description:
The subscription's one lifecycle fact (FIG-1951). The tagged enum makes
the five invalid `(enabled, tombstoned, deleted_at_ms)` triples a
window-79 peer could assert unrepresentable at decode.

oneOf.description:
A run's restore of the session's persisted tool state that some
persisted id had no registered source for (FIG-5134).

RemoteTurnCancelMode.description: The boundary at which a turn honours the cancellation request.

honoured_after_step.description:
The committed protocol iteration that honoured an after-step stop.
Absent for immediate stops and requests honoured before any step ran.

origin.description: Opaque host-domain data; Lash records and returns it unchanged.

duration_ms.description:
Whole-turn duration in milliseconds (claim → final commit). `0` when
the producer predates the field.

started_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock turn start (epoch milliseconds), measured from turn claim.
`0` when the producer predates the field.

RemoteTurnInputApplication.description:
Stable identity proving an admitted input became canonical turn input.

This wire DTO intentionally contains no display text. `input_id` and
`source_key` correlate to the admission receipt, while `turn_id` and
`committed_message_id` identify the canonical conversation application.

code.description:
The failure's namespaced code (`<namespace>:<spelling>`): `lash`
carries this workspace's [`TurnFailureCode`](lash_sansio::TurnFailureCode)
vocabulary, `provider` carries codes the provider emitted on the wire,
and host or plugin vocabularies keep their own namespaces verbatim —
never reinterpreted into a Lash spelling.

kind.description:
Typed origin of the failure. Serializes as the same snake_case string
the field carried before it was typed; an unrecognized spelling decodes
into `RemoteTurnFailureKind::Unknown` rather than failing.

provider_failure_kind.description:
Typed provider-failure classification, present only for classified
LLM provider/transport failures.

retryable.description: Typed retryability signal; `None` when the source did not know.

RemoteTurnIssueSeverity.description: Producer-selected effect of an issue on turn completion.

code.description:
The reason's code, as the park store keys it (`replay_divergence`,
`binding_drift`, ...).

profile_key.description:
The recorded model key the parked run could not bind, when that is
why its engine retries ran out.

RenderRefusal.description:
Why a protocol refused to resolve the render a run's results present
with. `refusal` is the protocol's own refusal type, serialized, and
`message` its display text.

RetiredProcessStatus.description:
The status a process row had when retention reclaimed it: the retired
subset of [`ProcessStatus`].

A tombstone and every "no longer retained" answer carry one, so a pruned
process still says how it ended: a `failed` one is never reported as
completed.

RetryClass.description: Evidence that permits another provider attempt.

RunCutRefusal.description:
Why a Run's frame cannot proceed: an earlier frame of its invocation
failed.

RunDefinitionRefusal.description:
Why a registered definition refused to shape a run: deterministic, so it
is recorded as the run's failure. `refusal` is the definition's own
refusal type, serialized, and `message` its display text.

RunInput.description: An input of the run that the worker reads when it starts.

RunRefusal.description:
The run's own inputs are refused. They are the same on every attempt, so
redriving the invocation refuses them again: the refusal is terminal.

RunShapeRefusal.description:
Why a run's shape was refused: deterministic, so it is the run's
recorded failure, carried typed as
[`RuntimeErrorCause::RunShapeRefused`](crate::RuntimeErrorCause::RunShapeRefused).

oneOf.description: The spec's registered definition refused its context.

A config owner refused the config the run's overrides derived, or
the options the run stated for it.

The reasoning the run would run is one its model's recorded
capability refuses.
The spec sets a reasoning selection for a session with no model.

The spec states protocol turn options for a session that records no
protocol plugin.
The protocol refused to resolve the run's render.

RuntimeEffectReplayMismatchReport.description: Compact, content-free mismatch evidence retained on the controller error.

effect_kind.description:
The kind of the recorded effect whose envelope diverged (its command
`type`, e.g. `llm_call`, `tool_invocation`), so an operator can tell a
model-call drift from a tool or cell drift (FIG-3587).

RuntimeErrorCause.description:
Typed cause retained when a controller-owned runtime effect must abort
through the generic runtime error boundary.

Attachment retention and worker causes keep their source's retry class.
Other causes are terminal except for an unavailable recorded model.

oneOf.description: Recorded material could not be read. This cause grants no body retry.

A callback returned state commands where no recorded body carries
their resolution.
A recorded callback's published state belongs to another owner.

A recorded state resolution does not follow its namespace's applied
frontier.

A namespace holds a reduced publication of unknown durability; it
publishes nothing more until the owner is rebuilt from durable state.
The attempt is not recorded: the invocation's recovery owns it.
A completed provider call's refusal, retained through plugin and host errors.
A typed worker failure retained through protocol and host errors.
A process start names a scope whose lifetime has closed.
A host start key already names a different start.
The attachment-store family and structured source of a required retention failure.

The identity of a submission refused for using another ingress kind's
reserved source-key namespace.
A durable record cannot be decoded. Retrying cannot repair its bytes.
A process row lacks the configuration its engine requires to execute.

A Lash object's compatibility record, or its absence, refuses this
build (ADR 0115 §3.2): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::EngineObjectStateFormatUnsupported`] when the
refusal is the object's, not one stored value's.

An artifact publish or acquire named a referrer that has a fence
(ADR 0113 §2.7): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::ArtifactReferrerEnded`].

The recorded model key this worker could not bind (FIG-4404).
A deployment serving the key repairs this retryable cause.

A tool call passed the session's recorded `max_tool_calls`
(FIG-4546): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::MaxToolCallsExceeded`].

Why a run's shape was refused (FIG-4652): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::RunShapeRefused`] and, for a refused reasoning,
of [`RuntimeErrorCode::ReasoningRefused`].

Why the config a session's creation stated was refused (FIG-4652):
the typed half of [`RuntimeErrorCode::SessionConfigRefused`].

The restore report of a turn run refused under
`ToolSourcePolicy::Require` (FIG-5134): the typed half of
[`RuntimeErrorCode::ToolSourcesUnavailable`]. Its lost members are
what no registered source resolves.

RuntimeOwner.description:
Who a runtime runs for: a session, or a process named by its minted id.

A session runtime and a process runtime cross the same interfaces — the
plugin session, the tool catalog, the attachment facade, the authority a
tool intent is declared under — and those interfaces take a
`RuntimeOwner`. A process runtime is never handed a session id as a
stand-in for its own identity.

ScopeId.description:
A scope a process may live until.

An effect opener (a logical turn run, a session operation, one process)
or a session. A session is never a tool Run opener:
it owns lifetimes, not effects.

oneOf.description: An effect opener's scope.
A session's scope, closed when the session is deleted.

SequenceFault.description:
A message that arrived out of order, or an exchange whose accounting does
not add up.

SessionHeadOwner.description: What owns a session's head, refusing a head write outside every run.

oneOf.description: An admitted run without terminal evidence.
An open session command, the earliest by `enqueue_seq`.

StartKey.description:
The idempotency key of one process start (ADR 0107).

A start key is never a reference: nothing resolves a key to a process. The
registrar maps a key to the process it minted for it while that process is
retained, so a retried start returns the retained process instead of
starting a second one, and after the process is pruned the same key starts
a new process with a new id.

A key lash derives from an admitted operation (a tool intent, a trigger
delivery) is trusted: a retry under it returns the retained process
whatever it submitted. A host's key (one it supplied, or its keyless
start's derived key) fences its start: a retry under it returns the
retained process only if it presents the same start, and is otherwise a
[`StartKeyConflict`](crate::runtime_error::RuntimeErrorCode::ProcessStartKeyConflict)
that names nothing but the key.

Every key is a framed digest in one family, with each start path in its own
namespace, so a host-supplied key can never collide with one lash derives
for a tool intent or trigger start. The digest is over admitted
operation identity only — never over submitted content, source or compiler
identity, or the minted result. Only [`StartKey::for_host`] is open to a
host; every other family is derived under a [`StartKeyDerivation`].

StoreFault.description:
A fault of the storage substrate that stays typed past the store, with
the same fields as its store error. A plugin error is cloned and
journaled, so it carries this rather than the store error: the identical
operation may succeed when it is made again, and nothing about it is the
operation's answer.

oneOf.description: Another writer holds the backend's write authority.
Another connection holds a database a whole-store migration needs.
The substrate failed the operation before it returned a value.
A backend failure with no typed cause.

StoreRefusal.description:
A store refusal that stays typed past the store, with the same fields as
its store error: a compatibility, session identity or cancellation
authority refusal. Plugin errors are cloned and journaled, so
this representation carries only the terminal refusals rather than backend
failures and sources.

StreamBlockIdentity.description:
Provider-minted identity of one streamed output block.

Minted by the provider adapter from provider facts: OpenAI
`(item_id, summary_index)`, Anthropic content-block index, or a
deterministic per-attempt ordinal for providers with no native notion.
The id is opaque to hosts; ordering comes from `ordinal`, never from
parsing `id`. Live and replayed streams emit identical identities.

id.description: Opaque provider-minted block key, stable within one response attempt.

item_id.description:
The reasoning or message item this block belongs to, when the provider
has one. N blocks may share one item's replay material.

ordinal.description: Per-attempt block ordinal assigned by the provider adapter.

StreamBlockKind.description:
Which render lane a streamed output block belongs to.

A *block* is the unit a host renders: one OpenAI reasoning summary part,
one Anthropic `thinking`/`text` content block, or one ordinal run of
thought/text for providers with no native notion. Blocks name their owning
reasoning item or message item when the provider has one; several blocks
may share one item's replay material.

oneOf.description: Visible assistant prose.

Reasoning summary ("thinking") text, kept separate from assistant
response text.

SupersededToolIdentity.description:
A persisted tool identity that a live id has replaced by owning its
model-facing name. The old grant is not transferred: the live id is a
default member and the retired id is dropped from the surface.

live_id.description: The live tool id that now owns the model-facing name.

name.description: The model-facing name both identities carry.

retired_id.description: The persisted tool id no source resolves any more.

SupervisorEvidence.description:
What the supervisor observed of a worker's end. Evidence, never testimony:
a worker cannot claim how it ended.

oneOf.description: The pipe closed with no exit status observed yet.

ToolAdmissionRefusal.description:
Why admission refused a call before any member of its round started.

One refused member admits no member: every call of the round answers
this refusal, the refused member with its own cause and every sibling
naming it.

oneOf.description: The tool's recorded declaration is itself invalid.

The call is declared isolated, and no process implementation is
bound to run it. An isolated call never falls back to an inline body.

Another member of the same round was refused, so this one does not
start either.

ToolCallLimitExceeded.description:
A tool call refused by the session's [`MaxToolCalls`]: the program asked
for more tool calls than its recorded limit admits.

It is the program's failure, never the host's: the limit is recorded
config and the count is a fact of the program's own history, so a replay
or a redrive refuses the same call. Nothing of the refused calls is
journaled or dispatched.

counted.description:
The calls counted against the limit before the refused ones: made so
far by a cell, held now by a process.

limit.description: The recorded `max_tool_calls` the execution runs under.

requested.description:
The calls refused together: one for a single call, an aggregate's
unique tool calls for an aggregate.

oneOf.description: A cell: the limit is the total it may make.
A process: the limit is what it may hold at once.

A member's declared execution is refused against the deployment's
execution budgets.

A result check proposed state commands outside the recorded body
that owns its decision. No command was reduced or published.

Admission refused the call, or a member of its round, before any
member prepared or started.

The body's outcome is one its recorded declaration does not admit: a
Deferred without `may_defer`, or an undeclared intent kind. Nothing
the outcome declared was realized.

ToolIntentCommandFailure.description: The typed command cause retained by a tool intent and carried to the host.

oneOf.description: A provider refusal retains the host's classification and namespaced code.
A process cannot run without the behaviour its creation recorded.
The process already accepted a different cancellation request.

A new start named a closed scope: its starter has ended, or the scope
its lifetime names has closed (FIG-3607 R11). The start is refused
before an id is minted, so the refusal names the start by its key.

A host start key is bound to a retained process another start made
(ADR 0107): the retry presented a different start. A host key is
global, so the retained process may be another originator's; the
refusal names the key and nothing of the process it is bound to.
Discovery must itself be an inline member of the tool catalogue.
A protocol's per-call batch maximum exceeds its hard ceiling.
An effective resident catalog member could not supply its immutable definition.

A catalog member's declared execution is refused against the runtime's
execution budgets: an inline-only tool declared above the ceiling.
An effective resident catalog member has no executable route in the pinned registry.

A fresh session create named an id the catalog already holds. A
create never adopts an existing session (FIG-4112); replaying a
recorded identity is a process run's `SessionTurn` initialisation,
not a create.

A lane-less head write found an owner in the store transaction.
Submit host head writes as boundary session commands, or retry once
the owner releases the head. The refused write changes nothing.
A plugin's config registration cannot stand on the deployment's plugin set.
An atomic plugin-state refusal, retained across journal transport.

A factory's [`super::PluginDeclaration`] failed the composition's owner
and format checks (FIG-4732): a session cannot materialize under a
plugin set that misstates itself, before any plugin callback runs.
A store compatibility refusal, preserved through plugin-facing ports.

The storage substrate faulted under a plugin-facing port: the identical
operation may succeed when it is made again, and nothing about the
fault is the operation's answer.

An existing plugin session cannot be reconstructed because a required
protocol-owned field is absent from its durable record.
A host attempted to substitute a durably pinned protocol selection.

A turn-scoped plugin write presented a lapsed or superseded borrowed
session-execution guard.
A session append operation id was reused for different semantic request content.

operation_key.description: Canonical durable operation key that was reused incorrectly.

session_id.description: Session whose append operation identity conflicted.

oneOf.description:
Durable append receipt metadata contradicts the retry's requested-node
count. This is store corruption, not a caller-recoverable conflict.

operation_key.description: Canonical durable operation key of the corrupt receipt.

session_id.description: Session whose append receipt is corrupt.

oneOf.description:
A durable plugin-owned record contained a value outside its declared
representation. Retrying cannot repair the stored bytes.

message.description: Backend diagnostic describing the malformed field or payload.

record_kind.description: Stable name of the durable record whose payload was unreadable.

oneOf.description:
A backend-owned authoritative clock produced a value before the Unix
epoch, outside the runtime clock contract.

A session-only operation ran under a process runtime. A process has
no session and no agent frame of its own, and is never handed its
originator's session as a stand-in.

An external or host completion named a stored attachment that has no
upload evidence: its source was ended and swept, so the output would
reference bytes nothing can read. Nothing is recorded.
An operation referenced a process id that the registry never knew.

A Process Change Feed cursor predates deletion history removed by
Tombstone Compaction. The consumer must perform a full relist before
resuming from the reported horizon.

The cursor predates retained subscription deletion evidence. Resync
through the atomic subscription snapshot before continuing.

A read of one process's events starts below the prefix its host released
(`release_process_events`). The events at or below the horizon keep
their sequence and replay identity but no longer carry their payload;
the reader resumes after the reported horizon.

released_through.description: The highest released sequence: reads resume strictly after it.

oneOf.description:
A recovery would end a process that a later segment already carries
(FIG-3820).
A stored wake-delivery row is keyed by an id other than the one its wake computes.

A process-registry continuation was passed to a backend other than the
backend that issued it.

ToolIntentKind.description:
Literal command kind of one recorded declaration.

Generated from [`tool_intent_variants!`]; never hand-edited.

ToolIntentRuntimeFailure.description:
The durable fields of a runtime command failure. Invocation-local retry
markers are not recorded command facts.

ToolRestoreReport.description:
Outcome of restoring a persisted [`ToolState`] over live sources: the
adopted generation plus what happened to each persisted tool id no
registered source resolved.

The three classes are different facts about the session, and only the first
is capability loss:

* [`lost_members`](Self::lost_members) — persisted `member: true`, nothing
  resolves the id. The session runs without a tool the host had curated
  in. This is what a host surfaces to its user and what
  `ToolSourcePolicy::Require` refuses a run on.
* [`parked_opt_outs`](Self::parked_opt_outs) — unresolved ids the host had
  already opted out of (`member: false`). Nothing the session could use is
  missing; the entry is kept so the opt-out survives the source's return.
* [`superseded_identities`](Self::superseded_identities) — an old id dropped
  because a live id owns its model-facing name. The capability is present
  under a new identity, which is a default member.

Entries in the first two classes remain in tool state as orphans and rebind
automatically when their source returns.

TraceAnchor.description: The span context a scope's first admission selected for its children.

oneOf.description:
No adapter was installed when the scope was admitted. Nothing invents
an anchor for it later; its cause is still retained for record
consumers.

The admission span's context. It may be unsampled: an unsampled
context is retained and propagated, which is not the same as no
telemetry.

TraceCause.description:
How an admitted operation relates to what caused it.

The first accepted cause is retained: a retry of the same business
submission under another context reads this one back, and an operation
first admitted as `Root` stays `Root`.

oneOf.description:
No cause: the operation starts a trace of its own. An adapter starts
it under an explicit empty context, never the ambient one.
The operation is an owned invocation of this span.

The operation is independently admitted work these spans communicated
with; it starts its own trace and links them.

omitted.description: Contexts dropped past the retained limit.

TraceScopeId.description:
A trace scope's identity: its owner and the owner's boundary ordinal.

Boundary 0 is the owner's admission. A later boundary of the same owner
(a process segment, a checkpoint that consumed new input) takes the next
ordinal the owner's own records already count. The id is separate from
every business identity preimage.

TraceScopeOwner.description:
The durable owner of a trace scope: the admitted thing whose work the
scope parents.

oneOf.description: An admitted run, the owner of its execution.
One physical agent turn, including a follow-on within a run.
One logical operation Run.
One tool call under its original logical owner.

One host-submitted tool intent, by its replay key, under the
runtime whose authority declared it: a session or a process.
A registered process, across all of its segments.
One accepted trigger occurrence.

TraceToolOwner.description: The logical owner of a tool call, independent of its execution route.

oneOf.description: The admitted logical run, whose turn id stays fixed across follow-ons.

TransportSequence.description:
The transport sequence: each direction numbers its messages from zero,
one apart, so a dropped, duplicated or reordered message is refused.

TriggerSubscriptionChangeCursor.description:
Position in one trigger store's subscription change feed. Never compare
cursors issued by different stores.

TurnInputAcceptanceReceipt.description:
Durable acceptance evidence returned to an ingress caller.

The receipt deliberately carries only stable routing and idempotency
identity. Queue dispatch and the pending row's mutable lifecycle state are
observed separately through the pending-input reconciliation surface.

VersionRange.description: The wire form of [`VersionRange`], before validation.

VmOwner.description:
Whose state it is: the session, or the durable process, the bytes belong
to. A worker is handed state only for the owner its lease runs under.

VmStateKind.description: Which VM state the bytes are.

oneOf.description: A suspended execution: a parked process segment or a suspended run.

A session's guest heap and roots between runs (the RLM worker
envelope).

WorkerDeploymentFault.description: Why this deployment cannot launch its configured worker executable.

WorkerFrameKind.description: The worker message an encoder refused, without its guest data.

WorkerLimit.description: The VM or worker limit a run exhausted.

oneOf.description:
A step's execution observations outgrew the run's heap budget, which
bounds the stream a worker holds and hands its parent, or a single
observation outgrew what one frame carries (FIG-4458).
The encoded effect request or result exceeds its configured bound.
A snapshot or continuation exceeds its configured bound.
A worker message cannot fit in one transport frame.

description:
The recorded answer to a sent input. Status and run are derived from
the variant's report or park, never stored beside them.

oneOf.description:
The run ended with a typed refusal no retry could change, and no turn
of it committed; `run` is absent when the engine refused the shift
before any run took the input. `refusal` keeps its typed code and
class: a runtime refusal is `error_type` `lash.runtime` with the
runtime error, typed cause included, as its payload, and a plugin's
own refusal is that plugin's failure.

The input was withdrawn before any run took it; its withdrawal is on
record, so a send under the same id answers this withdrawal.

Lash holds no record of the input: it was never accepted, or its
withdrawal was reclaimed. A send under the same id is accepted as new.
